correctness.rationale: The free-2-convex defining norm is converted exactly, by Hilbert contraction/nuclear-norm duality, into max over ALL edge-probability vectors of tr(sqrt(weighted Laplacian)); no finite truncation is assumed. Graph automorphism averaging follows from operator concavity of square root. Four invariant subspaces yield all positive eigenvalues, and strict scalar concavity together with inequalities at b=2a+1 and b=2a+2 establishes the cutoff for every integer a>=2,b>=1. An analytic pointwise witness distinguishes the compared elements. A separate executable checker verifies 36 exact rational spectra, 13 unrestricted numerical edge-weight optimizations and 15 admissible polar-factor norm witnesses. Numerical tests are not used as universal proof.

value.rationale: The explicit graph-edge lattice supremum is a natural operator-ideal/free-lattice invariant. The theorem solves an infinite integer family with a nontrivial positive-weight optimum, an exact sharp one-integer screening transition, and equality of norms for strictly pointwise-different lattice elements. The cutoff differs from the known same-graph determinant design, distinguishing two genuine spectral geometric mechanisms. Beyond finite computations and beyond a routine restatement of the bipartite formula.
